title: Multivariable Calculus
subject: Mathematics

cards.prompt: Define angle between vectors.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The angle in [0,pi] defined by cos theta=(u dot v)/(norm(u)norm(v)) for nonzero vectors.
required_concepts: The angle in [0,pi] defined by cos theta=(u dot v)/(norm(u)norm(v)) for nonzero vectors.
major_error_concepts: Using the angle formula when one vector is zero.

cards.prompt: Define Cross-product geometry. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The oriented vector in R3 perpendicular to both inputs with magnitude equal to parallelogram area.
required_concepts: The oriented vector in R3 perpendicular to both inputs with magnitude equal to parallelogram area.
major_error_concepts: Reversing order without changing the sign.

cards.prompt: State cylindrical and spherical Cartesian-conversion formulas, declaring your angle convention and the relation between the radii.
cards.definition: For cylindrical coordinates (r,theta,z), use x=r cos(theta), y=r sin(theta), z=z, with r≥0. For spherical coordinates (rho,theta,phi), take rho≥0, azimuth theta in a half-open interval of length 2pi, and polar angle phi measured from +z in [0,pi]: x=rho sin(phi)cos(theta), y=rho sin(phi)sin(theta), z=rho cos(phi). Thus r=rho sin(phi). Angles are nonunique on the axis and at the origin; alternative angle names are valid if explicitly defined.
required_concepts: Give the cylindrical conversion with radial distance from the z-axis.
Give a consistent spherical conversion and identify which angle is polar versus azimuthal.
Distinguish r from rho and acknowledge coordinate nonuniqueness.
major_error_concepts: The cylindrical radius always equals the spherical radius, including away from the xy-plane.

cards.prompt: Define Dot-product geometry. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The scalar bilinear product encoding angle projection and orthogonality under the Euclidean metric.
required_concepts: The scalar bilinear product encoding angle projection and orthogonality under the Euclidean metric.
major_error_concepts: Returning a vector or multiplying only matching nonzero signs.

cards.prompt: Define Line in space. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The affine set r(t)=p+t v generated by one point and a nonzero direction with parameter identity retained.
required_concepts: The affine set r(t)=p+t v generated by one point and a nonzero direction with parameter identity retained.
major_error_concepts: Using a second point as though it were already a direction vector.

cards.prompt: Define Orthogonal projection. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The vector projection of v onto nonzero u equal to (v dot u)/(u dot u) times u.
required_concepts: The vector projection of v onto nonzero u equal to (v dot u)/(u dot u) times u.
major_error_concepts: Returning only the scalar projection coefficient (v dot u)/(u dot u) when the vector projection onto nonzero u is requested.

cards.prompt: Define Plane in space. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The affine set of points x satisfying n dot (x-p)=0 for a declared nonzero normal n.
required_concepts: The affine set of points x satisfying n dot (x-p)=0 for a declared nonzero normal n.
major_error_concepts: Using the normal as an in-plane direction.

cards.prompt: Define Quadric-surface trace classification. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The identification of a three-dimensional level surface from coordinate traces signs and scale factors rather than name alone.
required_concepts: The identification of a three-dimensional level surface from coordinate traces signs and scale factors rather than name alone.
major_error_concepts: Calling every equation with three squared variables an ellipsoid.

cards.prompt: Define right-hand orientation convention.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The ordered-basis and boundary convention that fixes the sign of a cross product normal or circulation direction.
required_concepts: The ordered-basis and boundary convention that fixes the sign of a cross product normal or circulation direction.
major_error_concepts: Calling both normals equivalent when a flux sign is required.

cards.prompt: Define Speed and vector arc length. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The nonnegative norm of velocity and its integral over the specified parameter interval counting traversal multiplicity.
required_concepts: The nonnegative norm of velocity and its integral over the specified parameter interval counting traversal multiplicity.
major_error_concepts: Integrating component derivatives without taking their norm.

cards.prompt: Define Tangential-normal acceleration decomposition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The separation of acceleration into speed-change and direction-change components where curvature data are defined.
required_concepts: The separation of acceleration into speed-change and direction-change components where curvature data are defined.
major_error_concepts: Calling zero tangential acceleration zero total acceleration.

cards.prompt: Define Unit tangent and curvature. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The normalized velocity T and rate of tangent turning per unit arc length where speed is nonzero.
required_concepts: The normalized velocity T and rate of tangent turning per unit arc length where speed is nonzero.
major_error_concepts: Computing T when velocity is zero or confusing acceleration magnitude with curvature.

cards.prompt: Define Unit-vector normalization. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The division of a nonzero vector by its norm to retain direction with magnitude one.
required_concepts: The division of a nonzero vector by its norm to retain direction with magnitude one.
major_error_concepts: Normalizing the zero vector or dividing every component by their sum.

cards.prompt: Define Vector derivative. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The componentwise derivative r'(t) defined by the vector difference-quotient limit.
required_concepts: The componentwise derivative r'(t) defined by the vector difference-quotient limit.
major_error_concepts: Taking the derivative of the vector norm instead of each component.

cards.prompt: Define Vector magnitude and distance. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The Euclidean norm sqrt(v dot v) and the point distance norm(Q-P) with units preserved.
required_concepts: The Euclidean norm sqrt(v dot v) and the point distance norm(Q-P) with units preserved.
major_error_concepts: Replacing the Euclidean norm or distance by a signed sum of coordinate components.

cards.prompt: Define Vector-valued curve. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The parameterized mapping r(t) into Rn whose image orientation speed and multiplicity depend on its parameterization.
required_concepts: The parameterized mapping r(t) into Rn whose image orientation speed and multiplicity depend on its parameterization.
major_error_concepts: Eliminating t and losing traversal direction or interval.

cards.prompt: Define Velocity and acceleration. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The first and second time derivatives of a position vector with vector units and parameter meaning preserved.
required_concepts: The first and second time derivatives of a position vector with vector units and parameter meaning preserved.
major_error_concepts: Calling the scalar speed the velocity vector.

cards.prompt: State Clairaut's theorem, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** If the mixed second partials f_xy and f_yx exist and are continuous on a neighborhood of (a,b), then f_xy(a,b)=f_yx(a,b). Existence at one point alone is insufficient.
required_concepts: Both mixed second partials exist and are continuous on a neighborhood of (a,b).
Then f_xy(a,b)=f_yx(a,b).
Existence at one point alone is insufficient.
major_error_concepts: Assuming the symbols commute for every function.

cards.prompt: What is Clairaut's theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It licenses swapping the order of mixed partial differentiation under neighborhood continuity, but pointwise existence alone is insufficient.
required_concepts: It justifies equality of mixed partials under neighborhood continuity.
Pointwise existence alone does not justify the swap.
major_error_concepts: Commuting mixed-partial symbols without checking the theorem's hypotheses.

cards.prompt: Define Domain in Rn. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** For a function f:A subset of R^n to R^m, the domain is the declared set A; the natural domain of a displayed formula is instead the set on which its operations are defined.
required_concepts: For a function f:A subset of R^n to R^m, the domain is the declared set A
the natural domain of a displayed formula is instead the set on which its operations are defined.
major_error_concepts: Including the parabola where the logarithm argument is zero.

cards.prompt: Define Finite-path nonproof. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The boundary that agreement along any finite collection of paths does not establish a full multivariable limit.
required_concepts: The boundary that agreement along any finite collection of paths does not establish a full multivariable limit.
major_error_concepts: Calling axis agreement sufficient because the paths are perpendicular.

cards.prompt: Define Graph trace and level-set distinction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The separation among the graph in one higher dimension coordinate-plane traces and input-space sets where f has a fixed value.
required_concepts: The separation among the graph in one higher dimension coordinate-plane traces and input-space sets where f has a fixed value.
major_error_concepts: Calling a level curve the full graph.

cards.prompt: Define Higher-order partial derivative. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An iterated coordinate derivative whose order and evaluation point remain explicit.
required_concepts: An iterated coordinate derivative whose order and evaluation point remain explicit.
major_error_concepts: Reading the subscript order backward without stating a convention.

cards.prompt: Define Multivariable continuity at a point. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The conjunction that the function value exists the full multivariable limit exists and they agree at the point.
required_concepts: The conjunction that the function value exists the full multivariable limit exists and they agree at the point.
major_error_concepts: Claiming continuity from partial derivatives that exist only at the point.

cards.prompt: Define Multivariable limit definition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The full-neighborhood statement that f(x) approaches L for every domain point sufficiently close to a regardless of path.
required_concepts: The full-neighborhood statement that f(x) approaches L for every domain point sufficiently close to a regardless of path.
major_error_concepts: Checking one preferred curve toward the point.

cards.prompt: Define Open ball and punctured neighborhood. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The Euclidean neighborhood norm(x-a)<delta and its punctured form excluding the center for limit claims.
required_concepts: The Euclidean neighborhood norm(x-a)<delta and its punctured form excluding the center for limit claims.
major_error_concepts: Using coordinatewise intervals without reconciling them to one neighborhood metric.

cards.prompt: Define Partial-derivative field. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The function assigning a coordinate derivative to each point where that derivative exists, distinct from its value at one point.
required_concepts: The function assigning a coordinate derivative to each point where that derivative exists, distinct from its value at one point.
major_error_concepts: Supplying only a derivative value at one point when the partial-derivative function on its domain is requested.

cards.prompt: Define Partial derivative. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The one-variable derivative with respect to one coordinate while all other coordinates are fixed.
required_concepts: The one-variable derivative with respect to one coordinate while all other coordinates are fixed.
major_error_concepts: Differentiating y as though it depended on x without a specified relation.

cards.prompt: What claim does Partials-without-continuity counterexample refute, and why?
cards.definition: **Definition.** Define f(0,0)=0 and f(x,y)=2xy/(3x^2+y^2) away from the origin. Both coordinate partial derivatives at the origin are zero because f vanishes on both coordinate axes, but f(x,x)=1/2 for x not equal to zero, so f is not continuous at the origin and therefore is not differentiable there.
required_concepts: The false claim is that existence of both coordinate partial derivatives at a point guarantees continuity or total differentiability there.
A concrete witness is f(0,0)=0 and f(x,y)=2xy/(3x^2+y^2) for (x,y) not equal to (0,0).
Both coordinate partial derivatives at the origin are zero because f(h,0)=f(0,h)=0.
Along y=x the function equals 1/2 away from the origin, so it is not continuous and hence not differentiable at the origin.
major_error_concepts: Upgrading finite coordinate slopes to a full linear approximation.

cards.prompt: Define Polar limit bound. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The reduction to radius-angle coordinates paired with an angle-uniform bound that proves a full planar limit.
required_concepts: The reduction to radius-angle coordinates paired with an angle-uniform bound that proves a full planar limit.
major_error_concepts: Substituting polar coordinates and then fixing theta, which checks paths only.

cards.prompt: Define Two-path nonexistence witness. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** two admissible approaches with different limiting values proving that a multivariable limit does not exist.
required_concepts: two admissible approaches with different limiting values proving that a multivariable limit does not exist.
major_error_concepts: Averaging the path values and claiming limit zero.

cards.prompt: Define Vector-valued componentwise limit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The limit or continuity of a finite-dimensional vector output established exactly when every component has the corresponding scalar property.
required_concepts: The limit or continuity of a finite-dimensional vector output established exactly when every component has the corresponding scalar property.
major_error_concepts: Taking a vector limit by applying a scalar absolute value to the tuple.

cards.prompt: Define Chain-rule dimension diagnostic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The rejection of a derivative composition when evaluation points or matrix dimensions do not match the specified maps.
required_concepts: The rejection of a derivative composition when evaluation points or matrix dimensions do not match the specified maps.
major_error_concepts: Forcing elementwise multiplication to avoid the mismatch.

cards.term: Inverse function theorem and inverse derivative
cards.prompt: State the inverse function theorem for F:U subset R^n to R^n at a, including the derivative of the local inverse.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** If F:U subset R^n to R^n is C1 near a and det DF(a) is nonzero, then F has a local C1 inverse near F(a), and D(F^{-1})(F(a))=[DF(a)]^{-1}.
required_concepts: F is C1 near a and det DF(a) is nonzero.
F has a local C1 inverse near F(a).
major_error_concepts: Inverting a rectangular or singular Jacobian.

cards.prompt: Define Differentiability as best linear approximation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The existence of a linear map A such that the residual F(a+h)-F(a)-Ah is little-o of norm(h).
required_concepts: The existence of a linear map A such that the residual F(a+h)-F(a)-Ah is little-o of norm(h).
major_error_concepts: Checking only coordinate increments.

cards.prompt: Define Implicit differentiation in several variables. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The derivative relation obtained from F(x,y)=0 while retaining the condition that the solved-for partial derivative is nonzero.
required_concepts: The derivative relation obtained from F(x,y)=0 while retaining the condition that the solved-for partial derivative is nonzero.
major_error_concepts: Using an implicit derivative formula where the actual partial derivative needed for solving is zero, rather than checking that denominator at the stated point.

cards.prompt: Define Implicit-function rank boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The local solvability condition that a suitable derivative block is invertible or nonzero, without claiming a global graph.
required_concepts: The local solvability condition that a suitable derivative block is invertible or nonzero, without claiming a global graph.
major_error_concepts: Extending a local branch through folds without checking rank.

cards.prompt: What is the inverse-function theorem used for, and what does its local conclusion not establish?
cards.definition: The inverse-function theorem turns an invertible Jacobian of a C¹ map near a point into justified local coordinates and a local C¹ inverse. It is used to solve locally for inputs in terms of outputs and to analyze derivatives of the inverse. It does not establish global one-to-one behavior or a global inverse; a nonsingular derivative at one point without the stated neighborhood regularity is not the C¹ theorem.
required_concepts: Use: justify a local inverse or local change of coordinates from C¹ regularity and an invertible Jacobian.
Limitation: the conclusion is local, not a global injectivity claim.
major_error_concepts: A nonzero Jacobian determinant at one point proves the function is globally invertible.

cards.prompt: Define Jacobian chain rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The ordered product D(F composed with G)(a)=DF(G(a))DG(a) with compatible intermediate dimensions.
required_concepts: The ordered product D(F composed with G)(a)=DF(G(a))DG(a) with compatible intermediate dimensions.
major_error_concepts: Multiplying DG times DF because G is mentioned first.

cards.prompt: Define Jacobian dimension convention.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The readback that a map Rn to Rm has an m by n Jacobian acting on n-dimensional perturbations.
required_concepts: The readback that a map Rn to Rm has an m by n Jacobian acting on n-dimensional perturbations.
major_error_concepts: Reversing the output-row/input-column convention: for F:R^n->R^m acting on column perturbations, the Jacobian must be m by n.

cards.prompt: Define Jacobian matrix convention. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The coordinate matrix of DF with output components as rows and input coordinates as columns under the declared convention.
required_concepts: The coordinate matrix of DF with output components as rows and input coordinates as columns under the declared convention.
major_error_concepts: Transposing silently and then composing with incompatible shapes.

cards.prompt: Define Jacobian-vector product. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The directional first-order output change DF(a)v computed without treating the full Jacobian as the final perturbation.
required_concepts: The directional first-order output change DF(a)v computed without treating the full Jacobian as the final perturbation.
major_error_concepts: Taking a dot product of all matrix entries with all vector entries.

cards.prompt: Define linearization remainder.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The explicit residual between the true increment and derivative prediction with order or bound separated from the estimate.
required_concepts: The explicit residual between the true increment and derivative prediction with order or bound separated from the estimate.
major_error_concepts: Checking only that the residual itself tends to zero, which can hold for a poor linear map.

cards.prompt: Define Multivariable linearization. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The affine approximation L(a+h)=F(a)+DF(a)h with its base point and output dimension preserved.
required_concepts: The affine approximation L(a+h)=F(a)+DF(a)h with its base point and output dimension preserved.
major_error_concepts: Calling the affine approximation an exact identity globally.

cards.prompt: Define Scalar multivariable chain rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The derivative of f(g(t)) obtained by applying the gradient row to the velocity of the inner curve.
required_concepts: The derivative of f(g(t)) obtained by applying the gradient row to the velocity of the inner curve.
major_error_concepts: Differentiating z with respect to t while leaving x as an unrelated constant.

cards.prompt: Define Tangent plane from derivative. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The affine graph approximation z=f(a,b)+grad f(a,b) dot ((x,y)-(a,b)) when f is differentiable.
required_concepts: The affine graph approximation z=f(a,b)+grad f(a,b) dot ((x,y)-(a,b)) when f is differentiable.
major_error_concepts: Using partial values as intercepts rather than slopes.

cards.prompt: Define Total derivative linear map. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The unique best first-order linear transformation DF(a) from input perturbations to output perturbations when differentiability holds.
required_concepts: The unique best first-order linear transformation DF(a) from input perturbations to output perturbations when differentiability holds.
major_error_concepts: Treating the gradient column as though its action on h required no dot product or convention.

cards.prompt: Define Total differential. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The notation df=sum f_xi dxi representing the derivative linear map rather than independent finite errors.
required_concepts: The notation df=sum f_xi dxi representing the derivative linear map rather than independent finite errors.
major_error_concepts: Replacing finite Delta f exactly by df without an error statement.

cards.prompt: Define Boundary parameterization method. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The reduction of a smooth boundary component to a one-variable constrained objective with complete parameter interval and duplicate endpoints audited.
required_concepts: The reduction of a smooth boundary component to a one-variable constrained objective with complete parameter interval and duplicate endpoints audited.
major_error_concepts: Checking only t in an interval that misses part of the circle.

cards.prompt: Distinguish Candidate classification versus global conclusion.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Necessary equations and local second-order tests identify and classify local candidates, whereas a global conclusion requires comparing every feasible interior and boundary candidate and justifying global coverage through conditions such as compactness or global convexity.
required_concepts: Necessary equations and local second-order tests identify and classify local candidates.
A global conclusion compares every feasible interior and boundary candidate and must justify that the feasible search is complete.
Local classification becomes a global conclusion only with additional global coverage, such as compactness plus exhaustive comparison or a valid global-convexity argument.
major_error_concepts: Calling local convex curvature at one point global convexity.

cards.prompt: Define compact-region extrema candidate set.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The comparison of interior critical points boundary critical points corners and endpoints on a compact feasible region.
required_concepts: The comparison of interior critical points boundary critical points corners and endpoints on a compact feasible region.
major_error_concepts: Using only the interior gradient and concluding there are no extrema.

cards.prompt: Define Constraint-qualification boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The warning that the multiplier equation need not capture all constrained extrema where the constraint gradient vanishes or the set is nonsmooth.
required_concepts: The warning that the multiplier equation need not capture all constrained extrema where the constraint gradient vanishes or the set is nonsmooth.
major_error_concepts: Dividing by a constraint derivative that is zero.

cards.prompt: Define Critical point. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An interior domain point where the gradient vanishes or fails to exist, serving as a candidate rather than an extremum certificate.
required_concepts: An interior domain point where the gradient vanishes or fails to exist, serving as a candidate rather than an extremum certificate.
major_error_concepts: Calling every zero-gradient point a minimum.

cards.prompt: Define Degenerate Hessian inconclusive branch. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The requirement for higher-order or direct sign evidence when the Hessian test is singular or semidefinite.
required_concepts: The requirement for higher-order or direct sign evidence when the Hessian test is singular or semidefinite.
major_error_concepts: Calling zero Hessian evidence that the function is locally constant.

cards.prompt: Define Derivative information versus optimization guarantees. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The boundary that calculus defines local derivative objects while optimization and ML courses own algorithms stochastic estimates conditioning convergence and training dynamics.
required_concepts: Calculus defines local derivative objects.
Optimization and machine-learning courses own algorithmic, stochastic-estimation, conditioning, convergence, and training-dynamics claims.
major_error_concepts: Upgrading a symbolic gradient into a training guarantee.

cards.prompt: Define Directional derivative with unit direction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The rate D_u f=grad f dot u for differentiable f and a direction vector u of norm one.
required_concepts: The rate D_u f=grad f dot u for differentiable f and a direction vector u of norm one.
major_error_concepts: Using (3,4) directly and reporting a rate scaled by 5.

cards.prompt: Define Gradient vector. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The coordinate vector of scalar partial derivatives representing the derivative under the Euclidean inner product.
required_concepts: The coordinate vector of scalar partial derivatives representing the derivative under the Euclidean inner product.
major_error_concepts: Treating the gradient as a row Jacobian without declaring convention when dot products follow.

cards.prompt: Define Hessian matrix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The matrix of second partial derivatives with order convention and symmetry only under sufficient hypotheses.
required_concepts: The matrix of second partial derivatives with order convention and symmetry only under sufficient hypotheses.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every Hessian is symmetric without checking mixed-partial conditions.

cards.prompt: Define Lagrange multiplier equation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The necessary regular-point condition grad f=lambda grad g for equality constraint g=c, followed by feasibility and candidate comparison.
required_concepts: The necessary regular-point condition grad f=lambda grad g for equality constraint g=c, followed by feasibility and candidate comparison.
major_error_concepts: Solving the gradient equations but not checking the constraint.

cards.prompt: Define Level-set normal. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The gradient of a differentiable scalar field as a normal to a regular level set where the gradient is nonzero.
required_concepts: The gradient of a differentiable scalar field as a normal to a regular level set where the gradient is nonzero.
major_error_concepts: Using the gradient at a point where it vanishes and claiming a regular tangent plane.

cards.prompt: Define Quadratic form from the Hessian. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The scalar h transpose H h governing second-order directional curvature in the Taylor model.
required_concepts: The scalar h transpose H h governing second-order directional curvature in the Taylor model.
major_error_concepts: Reading diagonal signs alone for a single direction without computing the form.

cards.prompt: Define Second-order Taylor model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The value gradient term and one-half Hessian quadratic term around a base point plus a qualified remainder.
required_concepts: The value gradient term and one-half Hessian quadratic term around a base point plus a qualified remainder.
major_error_concepts: Omitting the one-half factor or calling the truncation exact globally.

cards.prompt: What is Steepest-ascent theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It identifies the gradient direction as the unit direction of greatest instantaneous increase, while making no global-optimality claim.
required_concepts: It selects the locally steepest unit direction.
It does not establish a global maximizer.
major_error_concepts: Treating a nonzero gradient direction as proof of global optimality.

cards.prompt: State the steepest-ascent theorem for a differentiable scalar field, including the zero-gradient case.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** If f is differentiable at a and grad f(a) is nonzero, then the maximum of D_u f(a) over unit u is ||grad f(a)||, attained at u=grad f(a)/||grad f(a)||. If grad f(a)=0, every directional derivative is zero.
required_concepts: For nonzero grad f(a), max over unit u of D_u f(a) is ||grad f(a)||.
The maximizing unit direction is grad f(a)/||grad f(a)||.
If grad f(a)=0, every directional derivative is zero.
major_error_concepts: Reporting grad f itself as a unit direction.

cards.prompt: State the two-variable Hessian determinant test, including all sign cases and its hypotheses.
cards.definition: Suppose f is C² near a stationary point c in R². Set D=f_xx(c)f_yy(c)-f_xy(c)^2. If D>0 and f_xx(c)>0, c is a strict local minimum; if D>0 and f_xx(c)<0, it is a strict local maximum. If D<0 it is a saddle point. If D=0 the test is inconclusive.
required_concepts: Apply the test at a stationary point of a C² function.
D>0 gives a minimum for positive f_xx and a maximum for negative f_xx.
D<0 gives a saddle; D=0 is inconclusive.
major_error_concepts: D=0 proves there is no extremum, and D<0 gives a local minimum.

cards.term: dimensional consistency of a multiple integral
cards.prompt: Define dimensional consistency of a multiple integral.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The reconciliation of integrand units Jacobian or measure units and target volume mass moment or average before accepting the result.
required_concepts: The reconciliation of integrand units Jacobian or measure units and target volume mass moment or average before accepting the result.
major_error_concepts: Accepting mass per length because only one differential was tracked.

cards.prompt: Define Double integral in polar coordinates. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The integral of f(r cos theta,r sin theta) times r dr dtheta over a correctly transformed planar region.
required_concepts: The integral of f(r cos theta,r sin theta) times r dr dtheta over a correctly transformed planar region.
major_error_concepts: Omitting the factor r.

cards.prompt: Define Double integral over a rectangle. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The limit accumulation over a rectangular planar region with signed integrand and area measure.
required_concepts: The limit accumulation over a rectangular planar region with signed integrand and area measure.
major_error_concepts: Attaching integration bounds to a variable inconsistent with the displayed inner differential or the declared rectangular region.

cards.prompt: Define Double Riemann sum. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The finite sum of function samples times subrectangle areas over a planar partition approaching a double integral under appropriate integrability.
required_concepts: The finite sum of function samples times subrectangle areas over a planar partition approaching a double integral under appropriate integrability.
major_error_concepts: Using a one-dimensional step width instead of area.

cards.prompt: Define First moments and centroid. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The paired coordinate-weighted density integrals divided by positive total mass using the same region and density specification.
required_concepts: The paired coordinate-weighted density integrals divided by positive total mass using the same region and density specification.
major_error_concepts: Using boundary averages for a nonuniform lamina.

cards.prompt: What is Fubini's theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It permits evaluation of a double integral by either iterated order under stated hypotheses, but does not license arbitrary order exchange for singular functions.
required_concepts: It converts a double integral to iterated integrals.
Order exchange requires the theorem's hypotheses.
major_error_concepts: Swapping integration order for an arbitrary singular function without checking hypotheses.

cards.prompt: State a first-course sufficient form of Fubini's theorem for a rectangle.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** If f is continuous on R=[a,b]x[c,d], then the double integral of f over R equals both iterated integrals, with either order of integration.
required_concepts: f is continuous on the rectangle R=[a,b]x[c,d].
The double integral equals both iterated integrals in either order.
major_error_concepts: Assuming arbitrary singular functions allow order exchange.

cards.term: Mass from density over one region
cards.prompt: Define Mass from density over one region. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The integral of nonnegative mass density against the correct area or volume measure with units preserved.
required_concepts: The integral of nonnegative mass density against the correct area or volume measure with units preserved.
major_error_concepts: Integrating density over coordinate intervals inconsistent with the lamina.

cards.prompt: Define Moment of inertia. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The integral of squared distance to a declared axis times density measure.
required_concepts: The integral of squared distance to a declared axis times density measure.
major_error_concepts: Using signed distance rather than squared distance.

cards.prompt: Define Order-reversal region reconstruction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The geometric derivation of new iterated bounds representing exactly the same point set after reversing order.
required_concepts: The geometric derivation of new iterated bounds representing exactly the same point set after reversing order.
major_error_concepts: Keeping x as an outer bound after making y outer.

cards.prompt: Define Triple iterated integral. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The repeated evaluation over nested bounds that encode one solid region and order.
required_concepts: The repeated evaluation over nested bounds that encode one solid region and order.
major_error_concepts: Multiplying unrelated coordinate ranges without checking the actual solid.

cards.prompt: Define Triple Riemann accumulation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The volume-element limit underlying a triple integral over a three-dimensional region.
required_concepts: The volume-element limit underlying a triple integral over a three-dimensional region.
major_error_concepts: Using area element dA for a solid mass.

cards.prompt: Define Type-I planar region. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The set a<=x<=b with lower_y(x)<=y<=upper_y(x) used to generate dy dx bounds.
required_concepts: The set a<=x<=b with lower_y(x)<=y<=upper_y(x) used to generate dy dx bounds.
major_error_concepts: Replacing the specified variable lower/upper vertical boundaries by an unsupported constant bound, thereby changing the Type-I region.

cards.prompt: Define Type-II planar region. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The set c<=y<=d with left_x(y)<=x<=right_x(y) used to generate dx dy bounds.
required_concepts: The set c<=y<=d with left_x(y)<=x<=right_x(y) used to generate dx dy bounds.
major_error_concepts: Swapping differential labels without reconstructing bounds.

cards.prompt: State the volume formula for a solid E and the equivalent height-over-base formula when applicable.
cards.definition: The volume of a solid E is the triple integral over E of 1 dV. If E lies between z=g(x,y) and z=h(x,y) above a planar region R, with h≥g, its volume is the double integral over R of (h-g) dA. The double integral over R of 1 dA is the area of R, not in general the volume of E.
required_concepts: A volume integral over a solid uses the volume element dV.
A double-integral volume formula uses nonnegative height h-g over the base.
Integrating 1 against dA gives area.
major_error_concepts: The double integral of 1 over a unit-square base is the volume of every solid above that base, whatever its height.

cards.prompt: Define Absolute determinant measure factor. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The magnitude abs(det DT) used for unsigned area or volume measure while determinant sign retains orientation information.
required_concepts: The magnitude abs(det DT) used for unsigned area or volume measure while determinant sign retains orientation information.
major_error_concepts: Using -2 as a negative area scale.

cards.prompt: State the one-to-one mapping condition required by the simple change-of-variables formula.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The simple change-of-variables formula requires T to map the parameter region onto the target and be one-to-one on the interior, up to measure-zero boundary exceptions. A nonzero Jacobian determinant is a local condition and does not by itself establish this global one-to-one requirement.
required_concepts: T maps the parameter region onto the target region.
T is one-to-one on the interior up to measure-zero boundary exceptions.
A nonzero Jacobian determinant alone does not prove global injectivity.
major_error_concepts: Assuming a nonzero determinant alone proves global injectivity.

cards.prompt: State the multivariable change-of-variables theorem, including its transformation, Jacobian, image, and regularity hypotheses.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** Let R be bounded with boundary of measure zero (a piecewise-smooth boundary suffices), and let f be continuous on T(R). If T is C1 on an open neighborhood of R, maps R onto T(R), is one-to-one on the interior up to measure-zero boundary exceptions, and det DT(u) is nonzero on the interior, then integral_{T(R)} f(x) dx=integral_R f(T(u)) |det DT(u)| du.
required_concepts: R is bounded and its boundary has measure zero; a piecewise-smooth boundary is a sufficient stated case.
f is continuous on T(R).
T is C1 on an open neighborhood of R, maps R onto T(R), is one-to-one on the interior up to measure-zero boundary exceptions, and has nonzero interior Jacobian.
integral_{T(R)} f(x) dx equals integral_R f(T(u))|det DT(u)| du.
major_error_concepts: Multiplying by det DT without absolute value or region conversion.

cards.prompt: What is Change-of-variables theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It transfers an integral to coordinates adapted to the region or integrand while preserving volume through the absolute Jacobian and explicit multiplicity conditions.
required_concepts: It transforms both region and integrand.
The absolute Jacobian and multiplicity conditions preserve measure.
major_error_concepts: Changing the integrand but not the region, Jacobian, or multiplicity accounting.

cards.term: Change of variables versus density transformation
cards.prompt: Define Change of variables versus density transformation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The boundary that calculus supplies a deterministic change-of-variables formula while probability owns normalized random-variable density transformations support and multiplicity claims.
required_concepts: Calculus supplies the deterministic change-of-variables formula.
Probability theory owns density normalization, support, multiplicity, and random-variable transformation claims.
major_error_concepts: Calling any nonnegative transformed integrand a probability distribution.

cards.prompt: Define Cylindrical volume element. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The three-dimensional scale dV=r dr dtheta dz with radial and angular bounds separated from height.
required_concepts: The three-dimensional scale dV=r dr dtheta dz with radial and angular bounds separated from height.
major_error_concepts: Using spherical rho squared sine phi in a cylinder.

cards.prompt: Distinguish Orientation versus volume scaling.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The distinction between determinant sign for oriented maps and determinant magnitude for unsigned measure.
required_concepts: The sign of a Jacobian determinant records whether a transformation preserves or reverses orientation.
The magnitude abs(det J) is the local scaling factor for unsigned area or volume.
A negative determinant indicates orientation reversal, not negative physical area or volume.
major_error_concepts: Calling a negative determinant negative physical volume.

cards.prompt: Define Polar area element. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The local area scale dA=r dr dtheta arising from the polar transformation away from its coordinate singularity.
required_concepts: The local area scale dA=r dr dtheta arising from the polar transformation away from its coordinate singularity.
major_error_concepts: Using dr dtheta and obtaining wrong physical units.

cards.prompt: Define Singular-Jacobian diagnostic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** If det DT(a)=0, the derivative is not invertible, so the inverse function theorem gives no local C1-diffeomorphism guarantee and the linearized volume factor vanishes; singularity alone does not prove that T is not locally injective.
required_concepts: det DT(a)=0 means the derivative is not invertible.
The inverse-function-theorem local-diffeomorphism guarantee is unavailable.
Singularity alone does not rule out local injectivity.
major_error_concepts: Dividing by zero determinant to obtain the inverse scale.

cards.prompt: Define Spherical volume element. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The scale dV=rho^2 sin(phi) d rho d phi d theta under a declared angle convention.
required_concepts: The scale dV=rho^2 sin(phi) d rho d phi d theta under a declared angle convention.
major_error_concepts: Omitting sin(phi) or using degrees without conversion.

cards.prompt: Define Transformation Jacobian determinant. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The determinant of the derivative of the coordinate map measuring signed local oriented volume scaling.
required_concepts: The determinant of the derivative of the coordinate map measuring signed local oriented volume scaling.
major_error_concepts: Using the determinant of the inverse map without inverting its scale.

cards.prompt: Define Transformed-region bounds. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The exact image or preimage inequalities expressed in new coordinates rather than copied coordinate extrema.
required_concepts: The exact image or preimage inequalities expressed in new coordinates rather than copied coordinate extrema.
major_error_concepts: Transforming only the integrand.

cards.prompt: Define Curl-zero local test. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The cross-partial or zero-curl necessary condition for a smooth conservative field, sufficient only with additional domain conditions in the standard theorem.
required_concepts: The cross-partial or zero-curl necessary condition for a smooth conservative field, sufficient only with additional domain conditions in the standard theorem.
major_error_concepts: Calling equality alone a global potential certificate on a punctured domain.

cards.prompt: Define Curl. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The oriented derivative vector nabla cross F in R3 or scalar planar curl under a declared convention.
required_concepts: The oriented derivative vector nabla cross F in R3 or scalar planar curl under a declared convention.
major_error_concepts: Taking F cross nabla in the opposite order without changing sign.

cards.prompt: Define Divergence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The scalar sum of matched coordinate partials measuring local source-like expansion under its physical interpretation.
required_concepts: The scalar sum of matched coordinate partials measuring local source-like expansion under its physical interpretation.
major_error_concepts: Adding every partial derivative including cross partials.

cards.prompt: Define Domain topology caveat for conservativeness. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The requirement that holes singularities and disconnected pieces be audited before upgrading local curl evidence to global path independence.
required_concepts: The requirement that holes singularities and disconnected pieces be audited before upgrading local curl evidence to global path independence.
major_error_concepts: Ignoring a singular point because it is not on the chosen path.

cards.prompt: Define Flow-line distinction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An integral curve r satisfying r'(t)=F(r(t)), distinct from the static field and from an arbitrary integration path.
required_concepts: An integral curve r satisfying r'(t)=F(r(t)), distinct from the static field and from an arbitrary integration path.
major_error_concepts: Calling every curve drawn through field arrows a solution.

cards.term: Fundamental theorem for line integrals: role
cards.prompt: What is Fundamental theorem for line integrals used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It replaces a line integral of a gradient field by a potential difference, proving path independence and simplifying conservative-field calculations; no endpoint formula follows without a valid potential on the relevant domain.
required_concepts: It replaces a line integral of a gradient field by a potential difference, proving path independence and simplifying conservative-field calculations
no endpoint formula follows without a valid potential on the relevant domain.
major_error_concepts: Applying the endpoint formula to a nonconservative field.

cards.prompt: State Fundamental theorem for line integrals, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** Let phi be C1 on an open set U and let C be a piecewise-C1 curve r:[a,b]->U. Then integral_C grad phi dot dr=phi(r(b))-phi(r(a)).
required_concepts: phi is C1 on an open set U.
C is a piecewise-C1 curve r:[a,b]->U.
integral_C grad phi dot dr=phi(r(b))-phi(r(a)).
major_error_concepts: Applying the endpoint formula to a nonconservative field.

cards.prompt: Define Gradient field. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The vector field grad phi generated by a scalar potential on a domain.
required_concepts: The vector field grad phi generated by a scalar potential on a domain.
major_error_concepts: Integrating components independently without reconciling cross terms.

cards.prompt: What is Green circulation theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It converts circulation around a positively oriented planar boundary into a double integral of scalar curl, allowing boundary and area calculations to check one another; orientation controls the sign.
required_concepts: It converts circulation around a positively oriented planar boundary into a double integral of scalar curl, allowing boundary and area calculations to check one another
orientation controls the sign.
major_error_concepts: Using clockwise orientation without changing sign.

cards.prompt: State Green circulation theorem, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** If D is bounded with piecewise-smooth positively oriented boundary and P,Q have continuous first partials on an open set containing D, then integral_boundaryD P dx+Q dy=double-integral_D (Q_x-P_y) dA.
required_concepts: D has the stated bounded, piecewise-smooth, positively oriented boundary.
P and Q have continuous first partials on an open set containing D.
integral_boundaryD P dx+Q dy=double-integral_D (Q_x-P_y) dA.
major_error_concepts: Using clockwise orientation without changing sign.

cards.prompt: What is Green flux theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It converts outward planar flux across a closed boundary into the area integral of divergence, giving the two-dimensional divergence theorem; it is distinct from the circulation form involving scalar curl.
required_concepts: It converts outward planar flux across a closed boundary into the area integral of divergence, giving the two-dimensional divergence theorem
it is distinct from the circulation form involving scalar curl.
major_error_concepts: Using the circulation form and planar curl instead.

cards.prompt: State Green flux theorem, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** Let D be a bounded planar region whose boundary is piecewise smooth and positively oriented: the outer boundary component is traversed counterclockwise and every hole boundary clockwise. If F=(P,Q) and P,Q are continuously differentiable on an open set containing D, then integral_boundaryD F dot n ds=integral_boundaryD (P dy-Q dx)=double-integral_D (P_x+Q_y) dA.
required_concepts: D is bounded with piecewise-smooth boundary; positive orientation means the outer component is counterclockwise and every hole component is clockwise.
F=(P,Q), with P and Q continuously differentiable on an open set containing D.
integral_boundaryD F dot n ds=integral_boundaryD (P dy-Q dx).
The boundary flux equals double-integral_D (P_x+Q_y) dA.
major_error_concepts: Using the circulation form and planar curl instead.

cards.prompt: Define Green's theorem hypotheses.
cards.definition: **Definition.** D is bounded with piecewise-smooth positively oriented boundary: the outer component is counterclockwise and inner components are clockwise. P and Q have continuous first partials on an open set containing D.
required_concepts: D is bounded with piecewise-smooth boundary.
Positive orientation is counterclockwise outside and clockwise around holes.
P and Q have continuous first partials on an open set containing D.
major_error_concepts: Orienting every boundary component counterclockwise in a region with holes.

cards.prompt: Define Line-integral orientation reversal. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The sign change of vector work or circulation under reversed curve orientation while scalar ds integrals remain unchanged.
required_concepts: The sign change of vector work or circulation under reversed curve orientation while scalar ds integrals remain unchanged.
major_error_concepts: Reversing the scalar arc-length integral sign as well.

cards.prompt: Define Path independence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The equality of line integrals between fixed endpoints for every admissible path in a domain, equivalent to a potential under appropriate conditions.
required_concepts: The equality of line integrals between fixed endpoints for every admissible path in a domain, equivalent to a potential under appropriate conditions.
major_error_concepts: Testing one closed loop and claiming global independence.

cards.prompt: Define Potential reconstruction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The integration and consistency process producing phi with grad phi=F on the specified domain.
required_concepts: The integration and consistency process producing phi with grad phi=F on the specified domain.
major_error_concepts: After integrating a partial derivative with respect to one coordinate, allowing an arbitrary nonconstant integration-constant function of that same coordinate, or failing to match the remaining gradient components.

cards.prompt: Define Scalar line integral. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The integral of a scalar field along curve length integral f(r(t)) norm(r'(t))dt independent of orientation for the same traversal multiplicity.
required_concepts: The integral of a scalar field along curve length integral f(r(t)) norm(r'(t))dt independent of orientation for the same traversal multiplicity.
major_error_concepts: Using dr as a vector and obtaining a vector answer.

cards.prompt: Define Vector field. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The mapping assigning a vector to each point of a spatial domain with dimension units and singular set retained.
required_concepts: The mapping assigning a vector to each point of a spatial domain with dimension units and singular set retained.
major_error_concepts: Treating arrows as a parameterized trajectory without solving an ODE.

cards.prompt: Define Vector work line integral. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The oriented scalar integral integral_C F dot dr=integral F(r(t)) dot r'(t)dt.
required_concepts: The oriented scalar integral integral_C F dot dr=integral F(r(t)) dot r'(t)dt.
major_error_concepts: Using norm(r') and converting work into a scalar arc-length integral.

cards.prompt: Define Work and circulation interpretation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The field-dependent energy-like or rotational quantity from an oriented vector line integral with units separated from geometric length.
required_concepts: The field-dependent energy-like or rotational quantity from an oriented vector line integral with units separated from geometric length.
major_error_concepts: Calling every vector line integral flux.

cards.prompt: Define Closed-surface outward orientation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The globally consistent normal direction pointing out of an enclosed volume, distinct from merely upward.
required_concepts: The globally consistent normal direction pointing out of an enclosed volume, distinct from merely upward.
major_error_concepts: Choosing one constant normal for the entire sphere.

cards.prompt: Define Curl-flux surface independence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The qualified equality of curl fluxes across surfaces sharing the same oriented boundary when Stokes hypotheses hold.
required_concepts: The qualified equality of curl fluxes across surfaces sharing the same oriented boundary when Stokes hypotheses hold.
major_error_concepts: Replacing an open surface for direct F flux, which Stokes does not equate.

cards.prompt: What is Divergence theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It turns outward flux through a closed surface into accumulated divergence over the enclosed volume and supports conservation arguments; an open surface must first be closed with any added flux accounted for.
required_concepts: It turns outward flux through a closed surface into accumulated divergence over the enclosed volume and supports conservation arguments
an open surface must first be closed with any added flux accounted for.
major_error_concepts: Applying the theorem to an open hemisphere without adding and subtracting the cap.

cards.prompt: State Divergence theorem, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** If S is a piecewise-smooth closed surface enclosing a solid E, S has outward orientation, and F has continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing E, then the outward flux of F through S equals the volume integral of div F over E.
required_concepts: S is a piecewise-smooth closed surface enclosing E with outward orientation, and F has continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing E.
Under those hypotheses, the outward flux integral of F through S equals the volume integral of div F over E.
major_error_concepts: Applying the theorem to an open hemisphere without adding and subtracting the cap.

cards.prompt: Define Flux integral. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The oriented integral double integral_D F(r(u,v)) dot (r_u cross r_v)dudv with the chosen normal convention.
required_concepts: The oriented integral double integral_D F(r(u,v)) dot (r_u cross r_v)dudv with the chosen normal convention.
major_error_concepts: Replacing the dot product by a norm and losing sign.

cards.prompt: Define Open-surface closure repair. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The addition of missing caps to form a closed surface followed by explicit subtraction with compatible normals.
required_concepts: The addition of missing caps to form a closed surface followed by explicit subtraction with compatible normals.
major_error_concepts: Calling the hemisphere closed because it has a circular boundary.

cards.prompt: Define Parameterized surface. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The mapping r(u,v) from a planar parameter domain to a surface image with grid curves multiplicity and boundary identity retained.
required_concepts: The mapping r(u,v) from a planar parameter domain to a surface image with grid curves multiplicity and boundary identity retained.
major_error_concepts: Giving only the implicit equation and no integration chart.

cards.prompt: Define Regular surface patch. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A parameterization whose tangent vectors r_u and r_v are linearly independent on the relevant interior.
required_concepts: A parameterization whose tangent vectors r_u and r_v are linearly independent on the relevant interior.
major_error_concepts: Checking only that r_u and r_v are individually nonzero.

cards.prompt: Define Scalar surface integral. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The unsigned accumulation double integral_D f(r(u,v)) norm(r_u cross r_v)dudv over a controlled parameterization.
required_concepts: The unsigned accumulation double integral_D f(r(u,v)) norm(r_u cross r_v)dudv over a controlled parameterization.
major_error_concepts: Using an oriented normal and allowing negative surface area.

cards.prompt: Define Stokes boundary-orientation rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The right-hand compatibility between a selected surface normal and traversal of its boundary.
required_concepts: The right-hand compatibility between a selected surface normal and traversal of its boundary.
major_error_concepts: Choosing clockwise because it is positive in an unrelated parameterization.

cards.prompt: What is Stokes theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It relates circulation around an oriented boundary to flux of curl through any compatible spanning surface, enabling surface replacement and orientation checks; it applies to curl flux, not flux of the original field.
required_concepts: It relates circulation around an oriented boundary to flux of curl through any compatible spanning surface, enabling surface replacement and orientation checks
it applies to curl flux, not flux of the original field.
major_error_concepts: Using F flux instead of curl F flux.

cards.prompt: State Stokes theorem, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** If S is a piecewise-smooth oriented surface with positively oriented simple closed boundary C and F has continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing S, then the circulation integral of F around C equals the flux integral of curl F through S.
required_concepts: S is piecewise smooth and oriented, C is its positively oriented simple closed boundary, and F has continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing S.
Under those hypotheses, the circulation integral of F around C equals the surface flux integral of curl F through S.
major_error_concepts: Using F flux instead of curl F flux.

cards.prompt: Define Surface area element. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The unsigned factor norm(r_u cross r_v) du dv accounting for local parameter-area scaling.
required_concepts: The unsigned factor norm(r_u cross r_v) du dv accounting for local parameter-area scaling.
major_error_concepts: Using the signed z component alone as area.

cards.prompt: Define Surface normal orientation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The choice between opposite nonzero normals made compatible with upward downward outward inward or boundary orientation requirements.
required_concepts: The choice between opposite nonzero normals made compatible with upward downward outward inward or boundary orientation requirements.
major_error_concepts: Normalizing and then forgetting which sign was selected.

cards.prompt: Define surface-patch multiplicity condition.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The requirement that patches cover the intended surface once up to acceptable seams and that overlaps are reconciled.
required_concepts: The requirement that patches cover the intended surface once up to acceptable seams and that overlaps are reconciled.
major_error_concepts: Assuming a nonzero area element prevents global double coverage.

cards.prompt: Define Surface tangent plane. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The plane spanned by independent parameter tangents or normal to a nonzero gradient at a regular surface point.
required_concepts: The plane spanned by independent parameter tangents or normal to a nonzero gradient at a regular surface point.
major_error_concepts: Using the position vector as a normal without justification.

description: A definition-recall course deck covering core concepts in Multivariable Calculus.
